"""Starting architecture: the main campaign's default policy (conv encoder, width 64, depth 2, ReLU,
no normalisation), rewritten as a candidate file. A 3x3 conv body, a 1x1 conv placement head
(one logit per brick type and anchor cell), and DONE and value heads on mean+max pooled features."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The starting recipe scored 0.068 on three seeds and 0.258 on one, so outcomes are bimodal and depend on seed luck. With the default recipe the budget is only 131k steps, which at 4,096 samples per update gives just 32 policy updates. That is very few PPO iterations for a 401-way action space. My main hypothesis is that the agent is short of policy updates. Two levers might fix it. One is smaller batches, which give more updates from the same samples. The other is fewer epochs, which the budget turns into more samples (2 epochs gives about 243k steps; 1 epoch gives about 426k). This round tests both levers separately and one combination, so I can see which one moves dev success. A clear gain would be a mean of about 0.2 or more on both seeds. Anything within ±0.1 of 0.116 is noise.
analyses.2: All six round-1 seeds scored exactly 0.0684 (35/512). So did three of the four baseline seeds. This points to one fixed attractor: a greedy policy that only solves the trivially orderable designs. It does not look like ordinary noise. Changing how throughput is spent (batch size, epochs, number of samples) did nothing, so getting more samples or more updates is not the bottleneck. The baseline seed that reached 0.258 shows that escaping is possible. The likely blockers are exploration and credit assignment. With gamma 0.95, the +1 exact-build bonus fades over a 41-step horizon, so the agent mostly chases the immediate fill reward. Order-dependent designs (overhangs) need delayed credit. This round tests whether a longer horizon (gamma/lambda), stronger exploration (entropy), or both together break the plateau. Any 2-seed mean clearly above 0.07 counts as signal, since the plateau value has been reproduced exactly every time.
analyses.3: Almost every run ends at exactly 0.068 on dev. That looks like a fixed policy, probably greedy filling, that only finishes the easiest designs. Runs that escape it reach 0.26–0.33: one baseline seed and one seed of ent_coef 0.03 (r2c2). So the outcome splits into two groups, and what matters is how often a seed escapes, not small gains. Changes to batch size, epochs and data (r1) and a longer horizon (r2c1) never escaped. Only more entropy did, once out of 2 seeds, which is suggestive but not conclusive. r2c3 mixed ent 0.02 with gamma 0.99 and 2 epochs and failed. The weaker entropy, the long horizon or the 2 epochs could be to blame. This round keeps raising entropy as the main lever: try the maximum ent_coef 0.05, and test whether ent 0.03 gets a higher escape rate with more fresh data (2 epochs) or a lower learning rate that slows entropy collapse.
analyses.4: Entropy is the only setting that has moved results. Every trial with ent_coef ≤ 0.02 got stuck at exactly 0.068 on both seeds, which looks like a greedy-fill local optimum. With ent_coef 0.03, 2 of 6 seeds escaped (r2c2, r3c2; r3c3 had none). With ent_coef 0.05, both seeds escaped (0.28 and 0.16), so it is the current best (r3c1, mean 0.219). Lowering lr to 0.0005 with entropy 0.03 failed on both seeds, so updates that are too slow may never get away from greedy fill. Gamma 0.99 lowered training success. The batch-shape and epoch changes in rounds 1–2 did nothing without entropy, but they have not been tested with strong entropy. Seed noise is large: a 2-seed mean can swing by more than 0.13. This last round therefore keeps ent_coef 0.05 and makes one more change per candidate to its learning speed, update count or data amount.
